subject: PO authority, issuance cadence & itemization guidance for Sage IT onboarding
messages:

Subject: PO authority, issuance cadence & itemization guidance for Sage IT onboarding

Hi Connor / Lauren,

Thanks again for helping us kick off the vendor setup for Sage IT — we're excited to get provisioning started. Before we complete the intake, procurement team needs a few confirmations about Redwood's PO process so we can align timelines and our internal approvals. Specific asks below: 

- Does Redwood require a PO for all invoices, or is there a threshold (e.g., >$5k)?
- Typical issuance lead time once vendor is set up and the invoice is received (standard SLA we should expect).
- Who at Redwood has authority to approve/sign POs at different dollar bands (for routing our internal approvals)?
- Preferred PO line-item structure: do you require separate lines for labor vs. software, taxes, and any GL coding rules?
- Any special fields we should include on the PO for remittance / tax / entity details.

I've attached our vendor intake form and a preliminary W-9 for the entity we'll be billing under. If you can provide a short checklist and a sample PO template or line-item guidance, we can get our ops team to format invoices to match Redwood's expectations.

Would you prefer a quick 20-minute call today to walk through this, or should we handle via email?

Thanks,
Emma Carter
Procurement Lead, Sage IT Solutions
emma.carter@procure.sageit.com
Attachments: vendor_intake_form.pdf, W9_SageIT.pdf

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Emma Carter <emma.carter@procure.sageit.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO authority, issuance cadence & itemization guidance for Sage IT onboarding

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below: 

- PO requirement: Redwood requires a PO for all vendor invoices above $5,000. For recurring subscription charges under $5k/month we can accept invoices without a PO if pre-approved by the account owner; exceptions must be documented.
- Issuance lead time: Once vendor setup is complete and we have a signed SOW or invoice, Procurement issues a PO within 3 business days on standard cases. If the request requires legal review or additional approvals, add 3–7 business days.
- Signature authority: For purchase commitments <$50k, Head of Procurement can approve. For $50k–$250k, VP Finance signs. Above $250k requires CFO sign-off and a brief exec approval.
- Line-item expectations: We prefer a clear itemization: description, unit (hour/license/month), quantity, unit price, extended amount, and a separate line for applicable taxes. For professional services we ask for a labor/service line plus an optional travel/expense line. Use SKU or internal code where possible to map to GL.
- PO fields: Please include bill-to entity name exactly as on the attached W9, remittance address, invoice number, and tax ID. If you have a preferred PO number, include it in the invoice reference.

I've attached our internal PO_issuance_flow.pdf and a short line_item_guidance.docx that shows an example structure we use. Next steps from our side:
1) Please confirm the exact billing entity and remittance details from the W-9 you attached (we need the company name as it will appear on the PO).
2) Send the first draft invoice using the itemization sample or use the template Lauren will share.
3) We'll run vendor setup in the portal once we have completed intake + W9; procurement will create the PO and share the PO number via invoice acknowledgement.

We can do a 20-minute sync today at 1pm PT if that helps — I can loop in Legal for any contract questions. Otherwise email is fine.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Sr. Manager, Vendor Operations
Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
Attachments: PO_issuance_flow.pdf, line_item_guidance.docx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PO authority, issuance cadence & itemization guidance for Sage IT onboarding

Hi Emma — adding a few practical notes from a PO preparation standpoint and attaching our editable PO template. High-level guidance we ask vendors to follow so invoices flow cleanly through AP: 

- Recommended itemization layout (three blocks):
  1) Services (description, period, hours or qty, rate, extended amount)
  2) Recurring licenses/subscriptions (sku, seats, term, unit price, total)
  3) Taxes/fees (taxable indicator and tax amount as separate lines)

- Line descriptions: include a short code (if you have one) in parentheses at the start of the description so our GL mapping can be automated (e.g., \"ENG-SVC-001: Integration support (20 hrs)\").
- Taxes & jurisdictions: Redwood pays taxes based on the remittance address on the PO. If you collect VAT or local taxes outside the US, note those as separate lines and supply supporting tax IDs.
- Coding & SOW references: If services are tied to an SOW, include the SOW number on each line. For time-and-materials invoices, include resource names and dates.
- Payment terms: Our standard is Net 45 unless otherwise negotiated and captured in the contract. If you require Net 30, flag that now so procurement can escalate.

Attached: SageIT_PO_Template.xlsx (editable). Please populate one sample invoice using the template and send back — we'll run it through AP validation and generate the PO.

Routing note (who signs): Connor's summary is correct. For anything requiring faster processing, indicate the urgency on the intake form and we'll attempt an expedited PO. Procurement contact for vendor setup: procurement@redwood.com.

If you want, I can drop a short video walkthrough of the template later today.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Procurement Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
l Lauren_bishop@redwood.com
